_instructions: One file for everything on the Updates page. Copy the block that matches what you're publishing, fill it in, save. 'type' controls which tab it appears under and how the card is drawn. For podcasts and webinars, this site never hosts the audio/video itself — put the real links (YouTube, Spotify, Apple Podcasts, Zoom recording, etc.) in 'links', and optionally an 'embedUrl' (a YouTube/Spotify embed link) to show a preview player right on the page. podcastSeries defines the show metadata; podcast items reference seriesId. Card images: 1200 x 800 px (3:2), WebP or JPG under 250 KB; keep text, logos and faces inside the central 80% safe zone. Optional per-item "imagePosition" field (any CSS object-position value, e.g. "top" or "50% 20%") controls the image focal point; default center. Optional per-item "time" field (webinars only, e.g. "10:00 AM CAT") shows the schedule line on upcoming webinar cards as "Live: <date> • <time>". Every item carries a unique "id" for stable referencing, deep-linking, and analytics.

items.title: Archetype 1: The Solopreneur (The Do-It-Aller)
items.excerpt: Believes no one can do it as well as they can, so they refuse to delegate. Growth stalls because the business can never exceed the founder's personal bandwidth.

items.title: Archetype 2: The Procrastinator (The Over-Planner)
items.excerpt: Endless strategizing, courses, and research instead of shipping and selling. Motion is mistaken for progress.

items.title: Archetype 3: The Perfectionist
items.excerpt: Waits for the product, pitch, or website to be 'ready' before shipping or selling. Misses market timing and feedback loops because nothing is ever good enough to release.

items.title: Archetype 4: The Visionary (The Idea Machine)
items.excerpt: Constantly starts new initiatives and chases shiny objects. Great at ideation, terrible at follow-through; the team is whiplashed and nothing compounds.

items.title: Archetype 5: The Firefighter
items.excerpt: Addicted to urgency and crisis. Feels productive putting out fires, so they unconsciously create or tolerate chaos rather than building systems that prevent fires.

items.title: Archetype 6: The People Pleaser
items.excerpt: Avoids hard conversations, keeps underperformers too long, and says yes to every customer request. Margins and culture erode because boundaries are never set.

items.title: Archetype 7: The Technician
items.excerpt: Loves the craft (coding, design, selling) and avoids the CEO work of strategy, hiring, and capital. The business stays a job, not an asset.

items.title: Archetype 8: The Controller (The Micromanager)
items.excerpt: Delegates tasks but not authority. Reviews everything, reverses decisions, and trains the team to wait for approval—killing speed and initiative.

items.title: Archetype 9: The Lone Wolf
items.excerpt: Refuses partnership, advice, or mastermind groups. Isolated decision-making leads to blind spots and repeated avoidable mistakes.

items.title: Archetype 10: The Status Seeker
items.excerpt: Optimizes for appearances (funding headlines, fancy office, title) over unit economics and customer value. Growth becomes a vanity project rather than a durable business.
